issues.detail: Hebrew 'כְּסוּס עָגוּר' means 'like a swallow/crane' (a bird), but Chinese renders '像被圍困的燕子' adding '被圍困的' (besieged/trapped) which is not in the Hebrew; the Hebrew has no word for 'besieged'.
Hebrew 'אֲצַפְצֵף' means 'I chirp/twitter' (a sound), but Chinese '我哀鳴' adds '哀' (mournful/lamenting) which is not in the Hebrew; the Hebrew verb simply means to chirp.

Hebrew 'עָשְׁקָה לִּי עָרְבֵנִי' means 'oppression is upon me; be my surety/pledge for me' (imperative 'עָרְבֵנִי' = 'be my guarantor'), but Chinese '受壓迫者求你為我辯護' renders 'עָרְבֵנִי' as '為我辯護' (defend me), which changes the meaning from 'be my pledge/guarantor' to 'defend/vindicate me'; also 'עָשְׁקָה' is a noun 'oppression' not '受壓迫者' (oppressed person).
